provenance.giver: lang/ru — patronymic formation from the father's given name: masculine -ович/-евич/-ич, feminine -овна/-евна/-ична/-инична; transliterated forms as they appear in English translations (Maude, Garnett)
provenance.note: A patronymic is worn by every child of one father and individuates nobody by itself (the T5 lesson: Katerina Ivanovna / Alyona Ivanovna are two heads). It is never the head of a name. These endings are a CANDIDATE class, never a verdict: Aldrich, Ivanov and Richardson all began as patronymics and froze into family names, so no ending and no length floor tells a patronymic from a surname. The consuming organ (eoreader7 name-spans.js) decides the way a reader does — by POSITION (the middle of given · patronymic · family) or by a STEM that is a given name the reader has established (Ivanovna points at an Ivan the material knows); a two-token name whose second token merely carries an ending and points at nobody stays given + family. minLength is the candidate floor, this prior's own declared parameter.
